book.aoa.atomic_dossier.tooltip: A field dossier for the Atomic Age of Ascension of Ages.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.welcome.name: Welcome
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.welcome.descript: What the Atomic Age is and how to survive your own success.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.welcome.where_yo: Atomic opens after the Atomic Disassembler handoff.

The Gilded Age ends when you finish the Atomic Disassembler quest. That quest grants the atomic stage. The Void Titan is a required Gilded proof on the way there, but the Titan kill alone does not open Atomic. This age is about energy itself: newly unlocked uranium and thorium sources, fuel pipelines that refine them, and reactors that scale from Create rotation to a fusion torus. The questbook walks the order; this dossier explains the ideas behind it. Items from later stages are intentionally hidden from EMI until their required age unlocks. If an item is absent from EMI, that is the progression system working, not a glitch.

Two rules keep you alive here. First, radiation is a real mechanic: it accumulates, it lingers, and it does not care about your armor bar. Build the hazmat rack before the fuel line. Second, the main fuel and reactor milestones are staged: the questbook walks you from Create-scale fuel into required reactor work, while optional reactor families and high-risk builds are marked as side depth. Build control and containment before you light anything.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.name: Mechanics
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.descri: The fuel economy, the reactors, the factories, and the war room.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.nuclea: Uranium, hazmat, and the Create-tier reactor.

Atomic opens at Create scale: mine uranium from the ore sources this pack enables, crush it, cake it, enrich it, and load Create: Nuclear's reactor for rotation. Mekanism's full hazmat suit is the baseline. The Nuclear Science, reinforced, and Alex's Caves suit quests may log one piece, but their text tells you when a full set is the safety floor.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.period: Chemistry, ore multiplication, and isotope infrastructure.

The Periodic Table chapter is the Atomic lab wing. It proves the Mekanism chemical chain, the Digital Miner, elite and ultimate circuits, storage, lasers, and cross-mod chemistry parts. The Digital Miner is filter-driven: set the target carefully and it becomes precise extraction instead of blind quarrying.

This lane feeds better fuel logistics, circuit substitutions, isotope work, and late storage, but it is not on the Chaos Gate checklist. The off-world isotope quest is a visible promise for the next age's rockets, not a blocker for Atomic. Build this lane when the reactor floor needs throughput or when the quest asks for a lab proof; finish dawn, chain, soul, war, prophets, and Geburah for the age handoff.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.fuel_p: One barrel of yellowcake feeds the main fission families.

The main fission fuel chains in this age pass through yellowcake. Create: Nuclear presses its own. Nuclear Science leaches it in the Chemical Extractor. Mekanism enriches it from uranium ingots. Create: New Age's thorium route is its own side path. In this pack the yellowcake lines pour into one barrel: the Nuclear Boiler accepts Mekanism's yellowcake exactly as it accepts NS's own.

From the boiler the line runs gas to centrifuge to enriched pellets, and pellets press into fuel rods in three grades. Spent fuel is useful, not harmless: label and contain rods, dust, and salts until the reprocessor can handle them. Add scrubbers and sirens before the reactor room becomes routine.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.three_: Create-scale nuclear work, fission, the MSR, and the fusion torus.

After Create-scale nuclear dawn, Mekanism's fission reactor becomes the first large FE reactor core: multiblock casing, fissile fuel, sodium loop, industrial turbine. Run it small until the logic adapter's alarms bore you. Nuclear Science's fission core arrives next, hotter and pickier, burning the rods your pipeline presses.

The Molten Salt Reactor uses liquid fuel, so a frozen plug is its primary shutdown mechanism. The fusion torus uses a thirteen by thirteen electromagnet structure. Distill deuterium from water at the Chemical Extractor. Breed tritium by running a filled deuterium cell through the fission reactor. For the age handoff, the checked Oritech proof is Critical Assembly. Fuel Assembly remains a separate Atomic lane milestone. Nuclear Science fission, the Molten Salt Reactor, and fusion are reactor-depth milestones.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.machin: Factories in six tiers and storage with no bottom.

Machine Soul is the factory chapter. The gate-signing proof runs through Oritech core and forge work plus the Hostile Neural large simulation line. Stock Mekanism climbs advanced, elite, ultimate as core chapter work; the More Machines and Evolved addons add basic lines for new processes plus dense and overclocked tiers past the official ceiling.

The same chapter closes the storage arc: MEGA's 256M components and cells, ExtraDisks' infinite tier, Cable Tiers mega parts, the assembler matrix, and spatial IO that stores the room itself. If the gilded grid was a library, this one is a horizon.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.mechanics.thresh: The war chapter builds a deterrent, not a campaign. Required war proof is narrower than the arsenal: forcefield base, tier-one launch control, and the nuclear warhead proof. Higher silo tiers, payload galleries, turrets, lasers, and MI explosives are optional armory depth.

The MekaSuit is the age's personal endgame: powered plate, a module rack for work, mobility, and life support, and the Meka-Tool that replaces your hotbar's left half. Install radiation shielding before you walk a reactor floor in it, and the hazmat rack retires with honors.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.recipes.name: Reworked Recipes
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.recipes.descript: Where this pack rewires the stock progressions.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.recipes.yellowca: Mekanism's enrichment line feeds the Nuclear Science boiler.

Out of the box the two nuclear mods ignore each other: the Nuclear Boiler's tag only lists NS yellowcake. This pack joins Mekanism's yellowcake to that tag, so the enrichment line you built in the periodic-table chapter feeds the apex pipeline directly. If a boiler refuses Mekanism yellowcake, something has broken this bridge; report it rather than working around it.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.recipes.circuits: Elite and ultimate tiers print in three flavors; the quests accept each.

Elite and ultimate boards exist in three flavors here: Mekanism control circuits, Electrodynamics circuit tiers, and Chemical Science's organic boards from the spin coater. The questbook's circuit quests accept any flavor where mods genuinely overlap. Standardize on one line or run all three; the recipes do not care, only your logistics do.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.recipes.silent_g: Azure Electrum and Tyrian Steel in the Oritech Atomic Forge.

Build the Oritech Atomic Forge. Process one Azure Silver block, one Light Weighted Pressure Plate, and one ender pearl for 300 processing ticks. The recipe produces three Azure Electrum ingots.

This is a pack-specific Atomic Forge recipe and it is the high-yield one. The crafting-table recipe for Azure Electrum, four Azure Silver ingots with two gold and an ender pearl, still works and still returns a single ingot. That native route is a Gilded Age route in this pack. Azure Electrum unlocks with the Gilded Age, so the crafting table is open to you a full age before the Atomic Forge is. What this pack does remove is the generic Alloy Forge alloying recipe for Azure Electrum and the Productive Metalworks molten alloying shortcut.

Process one Crimson Steel ingot, one Azure Electrum ingot, and one Prometheum ingot in the Atomic Forge for 400 processing ticks. The recipe produces two Tyrian Steel ingots.

Silent Gear's own route survives untouched. The Alloy Forge alloys one Crimson Steel ingot, one Azure Electrum ingot, a Crushed Shulker Shell, and a Netherite Scrap into four Tyrian Steel ingots. That native route is a Gilded Age route, because Tyrian Steel unlocks with the Gilded Age. The Atomic Forge recipe trades a Prometheum ingot for the Crushed Shulker Shell and the Netherite Scrap the native route asks for.

Cast and grade the Tyrian Steel head, assemble the pickaxe, and apply the Overgeared finish to the completed tool.
Where the wikis and this pack disagree.
NS machines unlock here, not where the wiki says.

Public wikis assume you can build Nuclear Science machines the moment you find uranium. In this pack every NS reactor, the Mekanism fission multiblock, and the uranium economy itself are locked to the atomic stage. If a recipe shows in the viewer but refuses to craft, check the stage first: the locks come off in chapter order, not wiki order.

The three NS reactors share one fuel pipeline but not one difficulty. Fission needs a water pool and respect. The MSR needs its salts mixed in the fuel preprocessor first; a dry start does nothing. Fusion needs the complete electromagnet ring and BOTH cells, deuterium and tritium, loaded before ignition. If a remote plant behaves strangely after you leave, check chunkloading before rebuilding the reactor.

book.aoa.atomic_dossier.capstone.chaos_c: Dawn, chain, soul, war, prophets, justice.

The age ends in Macabre's The Pit, an Atomic-locked dimension and boss surface. Valamon, Gomoria, Gargamaw, Baal, and Morphegor fall in order, each leaving a heart as proof. The gate checks the lane capstones, the five prophet hearts, Geburah's justice core, and the Alex's Caves boss ladder. After Geburah you fight Luxtructosaurus, then the Watcher, then Tremorzilla, and every kill in that ladder feeds the capstone. See the Bosses category for each Atomic-gated boss.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.name: Bosses
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.descripti: Where to find the bosses that gate the Atomic Age.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.malkuth.d: FDBosses: Gilded Age exam boss, one of the three Qliphoth.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.malkuth.p:
From FDBosses. Malkuth is one of the three Qliphoth bosses. You already fought Chesed back in the Industrial Revolution; Geburah waits in the Atomic Age. Malkuth is the required Gilded exam boss.

His arena generates in deep ocean biomes in the Overworld. Locate the Malkuth Arena, then summon him inside it with an Eye of Malkuth. Craft or acquire the eye during the Gilded factory lines and carry it to the arena.

The mod's developers recommend fighting Malkuth at night, so start the duel after dark. Bring full Gilded-tier gear and be ready for a long fight before you place the eye.

Malkuth cannot be hit directly. His divine armor negates normal damage, so you fight him through the cannons built into the arena. You are made weak to Fire or Ice, shown on your crosshair, and you may only fire the cannon that matches your current weakness. Match the cannon to the weakness, fire, and repeat while dodging his slashes, boulder volleys, and impaling spikes.

He drops the Fire and Ice Core, plus the Malkuth Trophy and the Emberfrost Gauntlet. The core is the kill proof the quest checks for.

Clearing Malkuth is the boss proof the handoff checks for, not a stage of its own. That proof is co-required into the Atomic Disassembler handoff, so this kill is part of what opens the Gilded to Atomic step alongside the Void Titan, the five factory lines, and the Chartered Arcana magic proof.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.chesed.de: FDBosses: Industrial Revolution exam boss, one of the three Qliphoth.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.chesed.pa: From FDBosses. Chesed is fought in the Chesed Arena, which generates in Overworld biomes. Summon it with the Eye of Chesed at the arena. Chesed is the Industrial Revolution exam boss, not an Atomic boss, so you cleared it two ages earlier. It appears here because the Chaos Gate turn-in accepts any of the three Qliphoth eyes: Chesed, Malkuth, or Geburah.
A merciful lord with roll attacks, robot armies, falling-block slams, and vertical electric rays. Clear the robots and dodge the blocks. Drops the Chesed Trophy.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.geburah.d: FDBosses: judge of the End arena (Atomic exam).
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.geburah.p: From FDBosses. Geburah is fought in the Geburah Arena, which generates in End biomes (alongside End cities). Summon it with the Eye of Geburah at the arena. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age. The kill drops the justice core, the proof the Chaos Gate line checks for; it does not grant a stage of its own and does not grant Otherworldly. Present the justice core at the Chaos Gate capstone after the required Atomic lanes to open Otherworldly.

A judge of sins with judgement balls, ray and laser strikes, earthquakes, and the justice hammer. Do not let your sins pile up; keep moving and interrupt the hammers. Drops Geburah's justice core. Turn that core in at the Chaos Gate quest to grant Otherworldly.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.valamon.d: Macabre: first prophet of The Pit.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.valamon.p: From Macabre. Valamon is the first of the five prophets in The Pit, Macabre's Atomic-locked dimension. Activate the False Idol Valamon spawner to begin. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age.
A corpse butcher with bone-spike waves and a gut whip. Dodge the waves and attack between them. Drops the Heart of Valamon, one of the five prophet hearts the capstone checks.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.gomoria.d: Macabre: second prophet of The Pit.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.gomoria.p: From Macabre. Gomoria is the second prophet in The Pit, Macabre's Atomic-locked dimension. Activate the False Idol Gomoria spawner to begin. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age.
A fleshmonger monk that clones and grasps with mori hands. Handle the clones and break free of the hands. Drops the Heart of Gomoria.
Macabre: third prophet of The Pit.
From Macabre. Gargamaw is the third prophet in The Pit, Macabre's Atomic-locked dimension. Activate the False Idol Gargamaw spawner to begin. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age.
A grotesque consumer that spawns maggots and minions. Suppress the maggots and keep damage on the consumer. Drops the Heart of Gargamaw.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.baal.name: Baal, the Motionless Calamity
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.baal.desc: Macabre: fourth prophet of The Pit.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.baal.page: From Macabre. Baal is the fourth prophet in The Pit, Macabre's Atomic-locked dimension. Activate the False Idol Baal spawner to begin. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age.
A motionless boss with whirlpools and malleus maleficarum attacks. Avoid the whirlpools and maintain steady damage. Drops the Heart of Baal, the fourth prophet heart.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.morphegor: Macabre: fifth prophet of The Pit.
From Macabre. Morphegor is the fifth prophet in The Pit, added by the Dead God update. Wake the False Idol Morphegor spawner to begin. Stage-locked to the Atomic Age like the other four.

The tyrant splits into copies when wounded, so clear the splits before they surround you. Drops the Heart of Morphegor, the fifth prophet heart. All five hearts feed the Perturbation that summons the Dead God.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.infernal_: Block Factory's Bosses: Overworld dragon tower.
Where to Find the Infernal Dragon

From Block Factory's Bosses. Ashlord, the Infernal Dragon, is fought at a Dragon Tower, a surface structure in temperate Overworld biomes (plains, jungles, savanna, swamp, windswept forests, and the like). Stage-locked to the Otherworldly age, where its quest sits in the Dragon Technology chapter. The towers generate long before that, so mark one on the way through and come back for it.

An infernal dragon with Ashlord Guards and flaming shooters. This pack runs it at 700 health behind 25 armor, up from the stock 250, with base damage raised a quarter. Clear the guards, manage the fire, and strike the dragon's windows. Drops Dragon Bones and the Ashlord Skull.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.capstone.chaos_c: Past the prophets, Geburah guards the justice core. The chaos gate accepts that core only after dawn, chain, soul, war, the silenced prophets, and Geburah itself are complete. The periodic-table lab lane is not on that checklist, but the Oritech Critical Assembly reactor is. Finish it, and the otherworldly stage opens, and the sky stops being a ceiling.

Most of Atomic Oritech is a fleet-scale hangar route, but one step is on the Chaos Gate checklist: the Critical Assembly quest, where you build the Oritech fission reactor. That reactor is required progression. The rest of the hangar route has its own capstone: cross-dimensional addon, magnetic field, plutonium, prometheum, tier-six processing, and the ultimate addon. Finish the whole hangar for stronger infrastructure; finish Critical Assembly, and the rest of the gate checklist, for Otherworldly.

book.aoa.industrial_codex.tooltip: Steel, crude oil, the first current, and the road to the Gilded Age.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.welcome.name: Welcome
book.aoa.industrial_codex.welcome.descri: Four waves of industry, from cast iron to the first current.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.welcome.where_: What the Industrial Revolution is and how it opens.

The Renaissance handed you rotation, steam, and the Industrial Revolution stage. This age adds the three things that age deliberately lacked: crude oil, a refining column to split it, and the first electricity generated from what comes out. Everything you build here runs on fuel you pumped and current you made.

Eleven chapters open across four waves and a finale. Wave one is the raw base and opens with the age itself: The Ore Refineries, Early Factory, and Magic Feedstock and the Spectrum Network. Wave two is the machine layer: Power Motion and Grid, The Nervous System, and The Industrial Complex. Wave three is applied systems: Pressure and Plastic and Hidden Equipment and Side Gear. Wave four is the deep places: Deeper, Darker, Otherside and the Undergarden Descent. The Netherite Citadel is the finale, and leaving it grants the Gilded Age. Items from later stages are intentionally hidden from EMI until their required age unlocks. If an item is absent from EMI, that is the progression system working, not a glitch.

Start anywhere in wave one. The Ore Refineries, Early Factory, and Magic Feedstock all hang directly off the Industrial Revolution stage with no gate in front of them, so all three are open the moment the age lands. Work one at a time or all three together.

Take The Industrial Complex the moment wave two opens. It owns the only crude oil in the pack, and its fifteen-step trunk feeds the Grid, PneumaticCraft, and most of the Gilded age after it.

Read the Mechanics category before you light your first blast stove. Fuel does not work the same way for every mod in this age, and the wrong fluid in the right machine is the most common wasted afternoon here.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.capstone.name: Capstone
book.aoa.industrial_codex.capstone.descr: The wave ladder, Obsidilith, Chesed, and the Gilded Age grant.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.capstone.leavi: Finish the four waves, then take the citadel.

The age exits through its waves, in order. Wave one proves the raw base: Steam Tier Complete in the Ore Refineries, The Foundry Proven in Early Factory, and Spirit-Bound Agitator in the magic feedstock network. The Industrial Concord needs all three.

Wave two proves the machine layer: Rotation and Current Joined from the Grid, Logic and Routing Complete from the Nervous System, and The Industrial Complex from the Create and TFMG trunk. Those three open the Wave Three gate.

Wave three proves the applied systems: Pressure Mastered and The Armoury. Those two open the Wave Four gate.

Wave four is the two deep dimensions. Return from the Otherside and return from the Undergarden, and a single capstone records both. The Netherite Citadel opens alongside wave four rather than behind it, so you can walk up to the finale while the deeps are still in progress.

Obsidilith is the citadel exam. Killing it grants the obsidilith_defeated proof and nothing else. It does not grant the Gilded Age.

Fight Chesed next. It is the required Industrial Revolution boss and the first of the three Qliphoth trials, and clearing it is a proof the finale checks rather than a stage of its own.

The finale quest fans in eleven proofs: the three wave one capstones, the three wave two capstones, Pressure and Circuits Complete from wave three, and from wave four the Warden and Both Deeps Answered, plus Obsidilith and Chesed. When the last one lands it grants the Gilded Age. See the Bosses category for where each fight is.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.name: Bosses
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.descrip: Where to find the bosses that gate the Industrial Revolution.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.netheri: Where to Find the Netherite Monstrosity

From L_Ender's Cataclysm. The Netherite Monstrosity waits inside a Soul Blacksmith, a forge that generates in the Nether across the crimson forests, warped forests, soul sand valleys, and nether wastes. Stage-locked to Industrial Revolution.

The boss stands on the arena floor when the forge generates. If you find it empty, the Monstrosity was already killed or never spawned. Craft an Eye of Monstrous from four lava buckets, two netherite scrap, two blackstone, and an Eye of Ender, then use it on the Boss Respawner block to call the boss back. The fight itself: a molten golem that charges, slams the ground, and hurls debris. Bring Industrial-tier ranged damage and keep mobile. It drops the Monstrous Horn and scatters ancient debris on death.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.gauntle: Bosses of Mass Destruction: Nether arena fist.
Where to Find the Nether Gauntlet

From Bosses of Mass Destruction. The Nether Gauntlet is summoned in the Gauntlet Arena (a Nether structure) by breaking one of the paired Ancient Carved Blackstone blocks at its center. The Blazing Eye is the Gauntlet's drop, not its key. Stage-locked to Renaissance.
A spinning, laser-charging fist boss with energized and normal punches. Dodge the spin and the laser charge-up. Drops Bosses of Mass Destruction reagents and spawns ancient debris on death.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.obsidil: Bosses of Mass Destruction: End obsidian boss (Gilded proof).

From Bosses of Mass Destruction. The Obsidilith is summoned in the Obsidilith Arena (an End structure) by using an Ender Eye on the Obsidian Altar, which consumes the Eye. The Obsidian Heart is not the trigger; it drops from the boss afterward as your proof. Stage-locked to Industrial Revolution. The kill grants obsidilith_defeated. It does not grant Gilded Age by itself. Finish Chesed and the required IR lanes, then complete the Iron Era Complete capstone to open Gilded Age.

An obsidian boss with teleport bursts, anvil-drop attacks, and energy waves. Keep moving and punish the teleport recovery. Drops Bosses of Mass Destruction reagents and spawns an obsidian pillar on death. The Obsidian Heart is the kill proof the citadel line checks for.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.valkyri: Where to Find the Valkyrie Queen
From The Aether. The Valkyrie Queen is the boss of the Silver Dungeon, found in the Aether dimension. Challenge her in her arena. Stage-locked to Renaissance.
A flying valkyrie who awards medals as you damage her and yields when beaten. Bring ranged options; the Valkyrie Lance helps. Drops the Silver Key to the Silver Dungeon's treasure.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.yeti.de: Block Factory's Bosses: snowy plains brawler.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.bosses.yeti.pa: From Block Factory's Bosses. Skor, the Yeti, lurks in a Yeti Hideout, a surface structure in snowy plains (Overworld). Stage-locked to Industrial Revolution.
A frost brawler with ice-slam leaps and a freeze wave. Stay mobile, dodge the leaps, and punish the recovery. Drops the Skor Gauntlet.
FDBosses: the required Industrial Revolution exam, first of the Qliphoth.

From FDBosses. Chesed is the required Industrial Revolution exam boss and the first of the three Qliphoth trials. Malkuth waits in the Gilded Age and Geburah in the Atomic. Craft the Eye of Chesed from four Sculk in a plus shape around an Eye of Ender in the crafting grid. Throw the eye and follow where it points, the same way you would track a stronghold, until you stand in the Chesed Arena out in the Overworld. Summon the boss there with the eye.

Completing this quest is the Chesed proof the capstone checks for; the kill does not grant a stage of its own and does not open the Gilded Age by itself. The Iron Era Complete capstone waits on the required IR lanes, Obsidilith, and Chesed together, then opens the Gilded Age.

Chesed cannot be hurt with a normal swing. During its Lightning Ray it summons Condensed Lightning crystals. Break one with an axe to become Energized, then stand at one of the arena's ray reflectors so the beam strikes the reflector. Each redirected beam deals one point of damage, and that is the only way through its guard.

Kill the monoliths as they appear. If any are still active when the finisher comes, the attack cannot be survived. Keep your eyes on the boss, because looking away invites its blinding gaze, and clear the robot adds between ray windows. Below half health it enters a second phase with faster, denser lightning.

The drop is the Lightning Core. Combine it with a weapon in a crafting table for a chance to call Chesed's lightning down on your targets.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.desc: Fuel rules, the TFMG trunk, pressure, and how wave gates work.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.name: Mechanics
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.sile: Blaze Gold at 3.0 bar and the Industrial tool cycle.

Build the Silent Gear Alloy Forge with the pack's steel-frame recipe. It opens compound-material work, and it is also the only way to make Tyrian Steel later. Blaze Gold itself does not need it. The plain crafting-table recipe, one gold ingot and four blaze powder, stays available from the Renaissance onward.

The Pressure Chamber is the cheaper route. At 3.0 bar it turns one gold ingot and two blaze powder into one Blaze Gold ingot, half the blaze powder the crafting table asks for. Watch the pressure gauge and set a safety valve so the chamber holds 3.0 bar instead of venting past it.

Melt Blaze Gold in Productive Metalworks and pour a pickaxe head through the reusable Silent Gear cast. Grade the cooled head, assemble the pickaxe, and finish the completed tool with quartz on the Overgeared anvil.

The final Industrial forging quest checks the finished Blaze Gold pickaxe and its recorded forging quality.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.theme.name: Theme
book.aoa.industrial_codex.theme.descript: What this age owns, and how its chapters open.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.theme.the_trun: Crude, refining, and the first current.

Every age in this pack owns one capability. The Industrial Revolution owns crude oil, the refining column that splits it, and the first electricity generated from what comes out of that column.

The tell that you are in the right age is a pumpjack standing over a scanned deposit with a distillation tower behind it. Before this age there was no petroleum at all. Rotation and steam carried the Renaissance. Coke and creosote carried the Medieval times.

The tell that you have wandered forward is chemistry. Aromatics, gas cracking, transformers, and the wide power grid belong to the Gilded Age. If a recipe wants a chemical reactor or a transformer, it is not yours yet.

This age runs two production halves that meet in the middle. The ore half turns raw ore into steel and machine parts through Immersive Engineering, Modern Industrialization, Oritech, and Mekanism. The fuel half turns crude into diesel and current through Create: The Factory Must Grow.

They meet at the Grid. The TFMG Accumulator that caps the Grid chapter needs an electric motor from the fuel half and a machine hall from the ore half.

Neither half finishes alone. That is why the Industrial Concord asks for all three wave one capstones before the machine layer opens, and why the Wave Three gate asks for all three wave two capstones after it.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.theme.three_wa:
The age does not open all at once, and it does not open one chapter at a time. It opens in waves.

Wave one needs no gate. The Ore Refineries, Early Factory (Immersive Engineering), and Magic Feedstock and the Spectrum Network all unlock the moment the Industrial Revolution stage lands.

Wave two is the machine layer: Power Motion and Grid, The Nervous System, and The Industrial Complex (Create and TFMG). Wave three is applied systems: Pressure and Plastic and Hidden Equipment and Side Gear. Wave four is the deep places: Deeper, Darker, Otherside and the Undergarden Descent, and the Netherite Citadel opens alongside them rather than behind them. The citadel is the finale you fight last, not a fifth wave you unlock later.
Why It Is Ordered This Way

Each wave needs the one before it. The Grid and the routing floor run on steel, heat, and spirit feedstock that wave one taught you to make. Pressure and Plastic runs on current the Grid supplies and on plastic that needs a heated processing plant.

The two deep dimensions come fourth because their gear sits at netherite parity. Undergarden utherium and Otherside resonarium are Industrial-tier equipment, not Renaissance souvenirs, and the Warden guards the way in.

The finale waits until last on purpose. The Netherite Citadel holds Cataclysm and Bosses of Mass Destruction arenas, and both expect industrial armour. Clear the waves, then walk in equipped.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.name: Mods of the Age
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.descripti: Which mod owns which chapter, and what each one is for.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.tfmg_owns: The only crude oil in the pack.

Create: The Factory Must Grow is the only source of crude oil in this pack. Nothing else scans for a deposit, nothing else runs a pumpjack, and every refined fraction you use in this age starts in its distillation tower.

Its home is The Industrial Complex chapter, and it runs as one long trunk with no shortcuts. Cast iron, a coke oven, a blast furnace, casting, the pumpjack, the tower, engines, a generator, cable, and an electric motor.

Treat that trunk as infrastructure for the whole age rather than as one mod's side chapter.

Other mods consume what TFMG produces. PneumaticCraft compressors burn its diesel, kerosene, gasoline, and LPG directly, because PneumaticCraft reads shared fluid tags. Oritech and Immersive Engineering read its crude through the same shared tags.

Modern Industrialization is the exception, and it is an important one. Its generators do not read tags at all. Read Fuel Is Not Universal in the Mechanics category before you plumb TFMG diesel into a Modern Industrialization machine.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.the_ore_h: Immersive Engineering, MI, Oritech, and Mekanism.

Early Factory is Immersive Engineering, and it is usually the first chapter a player finishes. You already own its coke oven from the Medieval age, so the blast furnace and the first steel come quickly.

From there it teaches wiring, the crusher, the metal press, and the multiblocks that make sheet metal and components. Its capstone fans in four proofs: the steel component hub, the refinery, the improved blast furnace, and a generator.

The Ore Refineries is three mods under one roof. Modern Industrialization brings its steam tier, from coke oven through steam blast furnace to boilers, the large tank, and the LV electric machines. Oritech brings its foundry lane. Mekanism brings the metallurgic infuser, enrichment chamber, and crusher.

All three make steel and all three want ore doubling. Pick one lane and automate it properly instead of half-building three.

Every steel variant in the pack feeds the same shared steel tag, so a downstream recipe accepts whichever one you made.
Where generated power becomes usable power.

The Grid chapter is where power stops being one mod's private resource. Create Addition trades rotation for FE in both directions with its alternator and electric motor. Electrodynamics adds its own voltage tier with coal, thermoelectric, and solar generators, plus a wire mill for cable.

The chapter caps on the TFMG Accumulator. Charge one and mount it as your reserve. That single block is the proof that generation, storage, and use are all yours.

PowerGrid content in this chapter is optional flavour. No required quest routes through it, so build it only if you want to.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.nervous_s: Storage, routing, and logic in one chapter.

Routing, safety, and memory share a chapter. Applied Energistics 2 gives the ME controller, drives, terminals, and the crafting CPU. Refined Storage gives a parallel network with its own controller. Integrated Dynamics gives variables, readers, writers, and displays.

Build storage before logic. A controller with a drive bay and a terminal solves your inventory on its own, and Integrated Dynamics can then read that network as live values instead of guessing.

Integrated Dynamics runs on crystalized menril, and menril trees are thin on the ground outside the Meneglin biome. The Mechanical Squeezer is the fix. It turns one menril log into a full bucket of resin and pays out extra crystal chunks the hand squeezer never gives. Dry the resin in a Drying Basin and the loop closes.

Note the ceiling on Applied Energistics. The crafting CPU is complete at this age, but the pattern provider and molecular assembler that actually run encoded jobs are locked to the Gilded Age. You build the brain here and switch it on later.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.pressure_:
PneumaticCraft opens in wave three and runs its own pressure economy. Air compressors pack air into a tube network measured in bar, machines draw pressure out of that network, and every machine has a pressure it will not survive.

Its payoff is plastic and printed circuit boards. The Thermopneumatic Processing Plant makes molten plastic from refined fuel, plastic feeds the board components, and the photolithography chain finishes the board.

Neither is optional flavour. Plastic and circuit boards are the components later chapters keep asking for, which is why this chapter also hosts the Wave Three gate.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mods.the_deep_:
Wave four is two dimensions that were reachable long before you were meant to farm them. Deeper Darker turns an Ancient City frame into a portal to the Otherside, a sculk world with resonarium gear at its bottom. The Undergarden is a cavern dimension entered by throwing a crafted Catalyst at a built frame.

Both are stage-locked to this age. Their gear sits at netherite parity, which makes it Industrial-tier equipment by the pack's own rule.

Deeper Darker runs city, then deep dark biome, then the Warden, then the Heart of the Deep, then the portal. The Warden comes before the crossing, not after it.

The Undergarden runs a three-metal ladder. Cloggrum breaks with a stone pickaxe and unlocks iron-grade tools. Froststeel comes out of shiverstone and needs that iron grade. Utherium needs the Infuser, and the Infuser needs dreadrock and rogdorium from the deepest layer, so build the machine before you chase the crystals.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.tfmg: Cast iron to electric motor, in order.

The TFMG trunk is one chain, and its first half builds a loop that pays for itself.

Craft cast iron, then a Coke Oven from cast iron around an industrial iron block. The oven bakes coal into coal coke and drips TFMG creosote. Craft two Blast Stoves and a Firebox, then raise the blast furnace shell with a charge hatch and an output block.

The stoves burn creosote to make hot air. Hot air plus crushed raw iron plus limesand runs industrial blasting, which yields molten steel, molten slag, and furnace gas. Cast the molten steel into ingots. Furnace gas then feeds the stoves, so from that point the furnace fuels itself and you can stop making creosote for it.

Craft a Surface Scanner and power it from below. Its top face lights the chunks around it that hold an oil deposit, and it needs a steady sixty-four rpm to read. Pipe down to the deposit, set the Pumpjack Base on the pipe, put the Hammer Holder behind it, build the connector and head above, join them with hammer parts, and glue the assembly together. A machine input with a crank above it drives the whole thing.

Lay steel pipe, a mechanical pump, and steel fluid tanks before you refine anything. Then build the tower: steel tanks as the base, the Steel Distillation Controller beside them, output blocks stacked above with industrial pipes between, and a heat source under the tanks.

Bottle diesel and kerosene, re-distill heavy oil for lubrication oil, then build a regular engine and its controller. The engine spins a crankshaft, the Generator turns that into current, cable connectors carry it, the Electric Motor turns it back into rotation, and the Accumulator stores it.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.fuel: Three mods, three different fuel rules.

Every mod in this age decides for itself what counts as fuel, and mixing the rules up is the most expensive mistake available here.

PneumaticCraft reads shared tags. Its fuel list keys on the common diesel, kerosene, gasoline, LPG, biodiesel, and crude oil tags, so any mod's diesel runs a PneumaticCraft compressor. TFMG output works with no extra plumbing.

Modern Industrialization does not read tags at all. Its generators use an internal list of named fluids. TFMG diesel is not on that list, and no amount of tag work will put it there.

TFMG reads only its own namespace. Its furnaces accept nothing another mod produced.

The LV Diesel Generator has exactly two legal fuels at this age, and neither of them is TFMG diesel. Use Modern Industrialization creosote from the MI Coke Oven you built earlier in the same chapter, or Immersive Engineering creosote from the Medieval coke oven. Both burn at the same rate.

The TFMG Blast Stove is closed in the other direction. It burns TFMG furnace gas or TFMG creosote and nothing else, so an Immersive Engineering coke oven's creosote will not light it. That is why the chapter has you build a second coke oven even though you already own one.

The Firebox is different again. It is a liquid heat source and its fuel list is TFMG diesel, kerosene, naphtha, LPG, butane, and propane, so it only earns its keep once the distillation tower is running. Butane and propane sit in the fuel tag but no recipe produces them yet, so in practice you feed it the four fractions the tower gives you.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.pres:
PneumaticCraft measures everything in bar. An Air Compressor burns fuel to pack air into pressure tubes, machines draw pressure out of the same network, and a gauge shows you the level.

Every machine has a danger pressure, and it does not warn you twice. Past that number the machine explodes and takes the tube run with it. Fit a safety tube module on the network and set it below the lowest danger rating anything on that run carries.

Your first compressed iron does not come from a machine. Drop iron ingots on the ground and set off TNT beside them. Once a Pressure Chamber runs, it makes compressed iron cleanly.

The Pressure Chamber is a sealed box of valve and wall blocks around a hollow space. Feed it pressure and it runs recipes keyed to a bar level rather than to heat.

Read the number a recipe wants and hold the chamber there instead of running it as high as it will go. Blaze Gold is the clearest example: at three bar the chamber makes it from one gold ingot and two blaze powder, half what the crafting table asks.

Add two Pressure Chamber Interfaces, one importing and one exporting, and the chamber runs hands-free without breaking its seal.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.mechanics.wave: What a gate node is and how it completes.

A wave gate is a quest with nothing to hand in. Its only task is a check on other quests. When every quest it names is complete, the gate completes itself on the next tick and the chapters behind it appear.

Gates stay hidden until their requirements are met, so an unopened wave looks like an empty stretch of the questbook rather than a locked door. If a chapter you expected is missing, the gate in front of it is still waiting on a capstone.

Gates pay experience only. They never grant a stage and they never hand you an item you need.

Wave one has no gate. The Ore Refineries, Early Factory, and Magic Feedstock hang straight off the Industrial Revolution stage. The old wave one node still sits in The Ore Refineries as The Industrial Charter, but it is a record now and nothing waits behind it.

The Industrial Concord sits in Power Motion and Grid and needs the three wave one capstones: Steam Tier Complete, The Foundry Proven, and Spirit-Bound Agitator. It opens the Grid, The Nervous System, and The Industrial Complex.

The Wave Three gate sits in Pressure and Plastic and needs the three wave two capstones: Rotation and Current Joined, Logic and Routing Complete, and The Industrial Complex. It opens Pressure and Plastic and Hidden Equipment and Side Gear.

The Wave Four gate sits in Deeper, Darker, Otherside and needs Pressure Mastered and The Armoury. It opens the two deep dimensions and the Netherite Citadel at the same time.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.recipes.name: Recipes and Chains
book.aoa.industrial_codex.recipes.descri: The chains that will not tolerate improvisation.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.recipes.steel_:
This age gives you three separate steel routes and you do not need all of them.

Immersive Engineering smelts steel in its Blast Furnace from iron and coal coke. You already own the coke oven, so this is usually the first steel you see. Modern Industrialization smelts it in the Steam Blast Furnace, built in fire clay bricks with a steam hatch feeding it. TFMG casts it from molten steel, produced by blasting crushed raw iron with limesand under hot air.

All three feed the same shared steel tag, so downstream recipes accept whichever one you made. Pick the route your chapter order reaches first, automate that one, and leave the others until you want their byproducts.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.recipes.crude_: The refining chain in the order it must run.

Crude oil is useless until it is split. Pump it, tank it, and run it through the distillation tower before you plumb it into anything.

The tower matches recipes by exact output count. It compares the number of Distillation Output blocks in the stack against the number of fluids a recipe makes, and runs only the recipe that matches. Six is the maximum. Crude has recipes making three, five, or six fluids, so a four-block stack distils no crude at all.

Build five. A five-stack splits crude into heavy oil, diesel, kerosene, gasoline, and LPG, and it is the widest crude split that still re-distils heavy oil into lubrication oil. Heavy oil re-distils at three, four, or five outputs, so a three-stack runs both feeds too, and a three-stack pours the richest lubrication cut. What three costs you is the crude side, which drops to heavy oil, diesel, and gasoline. A sixth block buys naphtha on the crude run and costs you every heavy-oil recipe, so raise it only alongside a second tower.

Tank every fraction separately, even the ones nothing consumes yet. Gilded chemistry comes asking for exactly the cuts you were tempted to flare.

Diesel drives the TFMG regular engine, and that engine's cylinder reads the shared diesel tag, so other mods' diesel runs in it too. Biodiesel does not. It sits on its own tag and the cylinder never reads that one. The engine spins a crankshaft. The Generator converts crankshaft rotation into current. Cable connectors distribute it. The Electric Motor turns it back into rotation for Create machines.

The Accumulator closes the chain by storing the surplus, and it is the Grid chapter's capstone.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.recipes.circui: The one chain with no alternate route.

PneumaticCraft fixes this order itself and there is no way around it.

Build the Thermopneumatic Processing Plant first. It makes molten plastic from LPG or biodiesel, and every route to the plastic item casts it from that fluid. Nothing else in the pack makes PneumaticCraft plastic.

Plastic then makes the empty PCB, the transistor, and the capacitor in the pressure chamber. Each of those three recipes consumes one plastic, so plastic is the real prerequisite, not the boards.

Take an empty PCB and expose it in a UV Light Box to set the pattern, then bathe it in an Etching Tank filled with etching acid. That gives you an unassembled PCB, and it is the only route in, because the alternative recipe for the same item needs an assembly line you cannot build yet.

One unassembled PCB plus two transistors and two capacitors makes the finished board.

Only now can you build the assembly line. Every assembly machine, the controller, laser, platform, and drill alike, consumes a finished board. The board is the gate and the line is the reward.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.loot.name: Loot and Structures
book.aoa.industrial_codex.loot.descripti: What opens at this stage and what stays shut.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.loot.whats_ope: Netherite opens, Gilded chemistry does not.

Open: netherite. Until you hold this stage, chest loot quietly swaps netherite swords, tools, and armour for their iron equivalents. That swap stops the moment the stage lands, so the netherite you find from here on is real.

Also open: the two deep dimensions and their gear. Undergarden utherium armour and Otherside resonarium armour are Industrial-tier by the pack's netherite parity rule, and both dimensions unlock in wave four.

Still closed: Gilded chemistry and the wide grid. Modern Industrialization's distillery and distillation tower, TFMG transformers, and the Applied Energistics pattern provider and molecular assembler all stay locked until the Gilded Age. Locked items are intentionally hidden from EMI until that stage is earned. This is the stage system working, not a missing mod or an EMI glitch. When the Gilded Age unlocks, EMI reveals those items and their recipes.
book.aoa.industrial_codex.troubleshootin: The two things that stall this age.

A wave gate that refuses to complete is almost always missing a capstone, not broken. Open the questbook, find the gate, and read the quests it lists. Each entry names a chapter capstone.

The gate completes on its own the tick after the last requirement is done. There is nothing to hand in and nothing to click.

If the chapter you want is missing entirely rather than greyed out, the gate in front of it has not completed. Chapters in this age stay hidden until their wave opens, so an absent chapter is normal progress and not a lost file.

A machine sitting idle in this age usually has the wrong fuel rather than too little power.

Modern Industrialization generators accept only fluids on their own internal list. At this age that means Modern Industrialization creosote or Immersive Engineering creosote. TFMG blast stoves accept only TFMG furnace gas or TFMG creosote. PneumaticCraft compressors accept any mod's diesel, kerosene, gasoline, or LPG.

If a fluid goes in and nothing happens, that is the rule you crossed.

Modern Industrialization multiblocks report Shape Valid on the controller, and nothing moves until they do. Hold a wrench to see which blocks are missing and where a hatch may go. A missing fluid hatch is the usual culprit, because most of the steam tier wants steam piped in rather than fuel dropped in.

TFMG structures report through goggles. The distillation tower shows its output count and heat level, and the pumpjack tells you when the hammer or crank is missing or the base faces the wrong way.

Read the readout before you tear anything down.

book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.tooltip: Boss guide for the Otherworldly age.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.welcome.name: Welcome
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.welcome.desc: Abyssal depths and the Sunken City.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.welcome.wher: Atomic ends when you finish the Chaos Gate capstone and receive the Otherworldly stage. Otherworldly is the offworld age: Launch Window, Strange Dimension Ops, Dragon Technology, The Stellar Grid, Digital Cosmos, then Beyond the Veil. The questbook walks that order. This codex covers the deep-ocean bosses that surface during the age, so use it as a boss companion beside the quest spine. Items from later stages are intentionally hidden from EMI until their required age unlocks. If an item is absent from EMI, that is the progression system working, not a glitch.

The Leviathan is this age's proof boss. Defeat it in the Sunken City to claim the Tidal Claws proof. The kill alone does not grant Ascension. Finish every required Otherworldly lane, then turn in Tidal Claws at the Beyond the Veil capstone to open Ascension. Scylla and Nerakyss the Kraken open up now as well. Both hang off the Leviathan on the ocean lane, and both are Otherworldly work rather than Ascension prerequisites. See the Bosses category for where to find each.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.capstone.des: OW spine, Leviathan proof, and the Ascension grant.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.capstone.lea: Offworld spine through Beyond the Veil, then Ascension.

Walk the Otherworldly spine in order: Launch Window, Strange Dimension Ops, Dragon Technology, The Stellar Grid, Digital Cosmos, then Beyond the Veil. Those lanes teach rockets, offworld ops, dragon tech, megascale power, and late digital infrastructure. The questbook marks each lane capstone. Finish them before you treat the Leviathan turn-in as the age exit.

The Leviathan is the age proof boss. The kill drops the Tidal Claws proof, not a stage of its own. It does not grant Ascension. The Beyond the Veil capstone waits until every required Otherworldly lane is done, then accepts Tidal Claws and grants Ascension. See the Bosses category for the Leviathan and the other deep-ocean fights.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.name: Bosses
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.descr: Where to find the bosses that gate the Otherworldly age.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.the_l: Cataclysm: abyssal predator of the Sunken City.

From L_Ender's Cataclysm. The Leviathan is summoned in the Sunken City, a structure in deep ocean biomes (Overworld), using the Altar of Abyss. It is invincible outside of water, so fight it in its pool. Stage-locked to Otherworldly. The kill drops the Tidal Claws proof, not a stage of its own. It does not grant Ascension.

A multidimensional abyssal predator with tentacle strikes, bites, and roars. Stay in the water arena and dodge the tentacles. Drops Cataclysm leviathan reagents including Tidal Claws; its defeat also lets Coral Golems appear in the ocean. Turn Tidal Claws in at the Beyond the Veil capstone after every required Otherworldly lane to grant Ascension.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.scyll: Cataclysm: Storm Empress of the Acropolis, Otherworldly ocean lane.

From L_Ender's Cataclysm. Scylla, the Storm Empress, is found at the Acropolis, a ruin that stands over warm ocean (Overworld). An Eye of Storm points to it if the search runs long. Her quest sits on the Otherworldly ocean lane, behind the Leviathan and ahead of the Kraken. She is not an Ascension prerequisite.
A storm empress with howls and azure-seastone arena attacks. Weather the storm and keep pressure on. Drops Cataclysm scylla reagents.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.krake: Block Factory's Bosses: the end of the Otherworldly ocean lane.

From Block Factory's Bosses. Nerakyss, the Kraken, is summoned from a Kraken Spawner aboard a Kraken Ship, a wreck that generates in deep ocean, deep cold ocean, and deep lukewarm ocean (Overworld). Its quest closes the Otherworldly ocean lane, behind Scylla. It is not an Ascension prerequisite.

A tentacled abyssal boss with cannon and tentacle-smash attacks. This pack runs it at 900 health behind 20 armor, up from the stock 500, with base damage raised a quarter. Manage the tentacles and the cannon fire, and fight from the deck rather than the water. Drops the Kraken Tooth and Kraken Trident.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.dead_: Macabre: the god the false prophets served.

From Macabre. Once all five prophets are dead, ring their hearts around four Abhorrent crystals to craft the Perturbation. Using it pulls you into The Pit and calls the Dead God. Gated to the Otherworldly age, so the hearts wait until you have crossed over.

The Dead God borrows the powers of all five prophets, cycling through their attacks. Read which prophet it wears and strike in the gaps. When it dies it leaves a Dead God Egg on the ground, and that egg is the door to Limbo.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.meshu: Macabre: the hidden god beyond Limbo.
From Macabre. The Dead God Egg cracks after three nights. Right click the cracked egg to fall into Limbo. Kill the Shadows there for Black Chalk, then press four pieces into a Tabula Rasa.

Use the Tabula Rasa on a living Shadow to summon Meshuggeneh, the hidden god behind the false five. It is the terminal boss of the Macabre road and the last required Otherworldly proof. The same Tabula Rasa also teleports you home.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.sandw: Block Factory's Bosses: required Otherworldly kill, fightable from Renaissance on.

From Block Factory's Bosses. Sirok, the Sandworm, lurks in a Sandworm Nest, a surface structure in desert biomes of the Overworld. The nest is enterable starting the Renaissance age, but Sirok's kill is a required Otherworldly task. You fight it in the Beyond the Veil chapter, right before the Void Worm.

Sirok dives underground, then surfaces to bite, charge, and spit poison. Watch for the surfacing telegraph and punish the exposed head while it is above ground. Defeat drops the Sirok Gauntlet, a glove that shoots poison on hold-right-click.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.bosses.void_: Alex's Mobs: interdimensional parasite beneath the End, required Otherworldly kill.

From Alex's Mobs. The Void Worm dwells in the void beneath the End. Bait it out by tossing a Mysterious Worm into that void. You get a Mysterious Worm by placing a Mosquito Larva inside an Enderiophage's Capsid and letting it grow. This is a required Otherworldly kill, fought in Beyond the Veil right after Sirok.

The worm fires homing crystal shots, bites, and can tear open portals to reach hidden prey. Its body segments split the worm in two if you destroy them, so focus damage on the head instead. A kill drops an eye and mandibles. Combine two mandibles into a Void Worm Beak, or use the eye with mandibles and netherite for the Dimensional Carver, a pickaxe that tears a short-lived portal home.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.space_progra: Space Program
The Stellaris rocket, orbit, and the planet ladder.
Launch Window
Stellaris: build the rocket and reach orbit.
Building the Rocket

Launch Window is the Otherworldly age's opening chapter. Build a Rocket Launch Pad and a Rocket Engine, then work through the Oxygen Distributor and Fuel Refinery so you have air and fuel on tap. A Space Suit, an Oxygen Tank, and Jet Suit pieces come before the rocket itself; you need them to survive outside the Overworld.

Fuel the rocket with refined Stellaris fuel and top off the oxygen tank before you launch. Both are required or the rocket will not fly.
Reaching Orbit

The first launch reaches Earth Orbit, a Stellaris dimension sitting above the Overworld. From there the chapter keeps going outward. See The Planet Ladder in this category for what comes after Earth Orbit.
The Planet Ladder
Stellaris: Moon, then Mercury, Venus, and Mars.
The Moon First

After Earth Orbit, Launch Window sends you to the Moon, the next stop up the Stellaris dimension ladder. Landing there and finishing its tasks is what opens the rest of the solar system, so treat the Moon as a gate, not a detour.
Mercury, Venus, Mars

Once the Moon is done, Mercury, Venus, and Mars all open together. Each planet is its own Stellaris dimension with an orbit stop above it, so you can scout from orbit before you land. There is no required order between the three; work them in whatever sequence suits your rocket range and supplies.
The Stellar Grid
The chapter after Dragon Technology: megascale power and late digital infrastructure.
What The Stellar Grid Covers

The Stellar Grid is the Otherworldly chapter that follows Dragon Technology. It is not a Stellaris planet stop. It is where the age's power and storage tech tops out: Modern Industrialization's Superconductor Storage Unit, Ballistix antimatter production, AE2's quantum network gear, and Evolved Mekanism's multiversal factories all sit in this chapter.

This is late-chapter infrastructure, not an early task. Expect real setup time and real resources; it builds the power and storage base the rest of the age's machines lean on.
Where It Sits in the Spine

Walk the Otherworldly spine in order: Launch Window, Strange Dimension Ops, Dragon Technology, The Stellar Grid, Digital Cosmos, then Beyond the Veil. The questbook marks each lane's capstone. Finish The Stellar Grid before you treat the Leviathan turn-in as the age exit.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.draconic_fou: Draconic Evolution's early item ladder, taught in Dragon Technology.
Draconic Evolution's early item ladder, taught in Dragon Technology.

Dragon Technology opens with draconium. Smelt Draconium Dust into Draconium Ingots, then combine ingots into a Draconium Core. That core upgrades into a Wyvern Core, the next tier up Draconic Evolution's item ladder.

Each core feeds a matching Crafting Injector: the Draconium Core builds toward the Crafting Core, and the Wyvern Core builds the Wyvern Crafting Injector. Slot these into your Draconic crafting setup to unlock the mod's higher-tier recipes.

After the injectors, the chapter moves to power storage: an Energy Core paired with an Energy Core Stabilizer and an Energy Pylon, Draconic Evolution's endgame RF storage and transfer blocks.

The chapter capstone is the Energy Transfuser. Craft it to close out Dragon Technology. It is the last stop on the Wyvern tier before the ladder resumes at the Awakened tier much later, for the reactor build.
Where the Wyvern-tier ladder leads, later in Ascension.

Dragon Technology stops at the Wyvern tier and the Energy Transfuser. That is not the end of Draconic Evolution's ladder, just where the Otherworldly age leaves it. Ascension's Impossible Machine chapter picks the tier back up with Awakened Draconium, the Draconic Fusion Crafting Injector, and a Draconic Energy Core.

None of that is needed here. Finish this chapter's ladder first. What you build now is the foundation the Awakened tier sits on top of.

The Awakened tier feeds into the Draconic Reactor, a required Ascension win-gate multiblock built from a Reactor Core, a Reactor Energy Injector, and four Reactor Stabilizers, fueled by Awakened Draconium. See the Ascension Codex's Reactor category for the full build order when you reach it.
book.aoa.otherworldly_codex.mechanics.si: Tier-three charging for the prepared Tyrian Steel part.

Build the Silent Gear Starlight Charger where it can see open sky. It only gathers starlight at night, so a charger that shows no progress at noon is working correctly. Set it up and let a full night pass before you judge it.

Every tier needs the same four pillars, and the block you use sets the tier the charger can reach. Crimson Steel blocks give tier one, Azure Electrum blocks give tier two, Tyrian Steel blocks give tier three. With no pillars the structure level is zero and nothing charges at all.

Each pillar sits two blocks above the charger, three blocks north or south and three blocks west or east, so they mark the four diagonal corners of a seven by seven square. Put a Tyrian Steel block at every one of those four spots. The charger takes the lowest of the four as its structure level, so one missing or weaker corner caps the whole thing. The Structure Level readout in its interface confirms what it actually sees.

Moonstone Core and Hellforged Ingot are both registered as tier-three catalyst options in this pack, on top of the native starmetal dust. Hellforged Ingot is the craftable one, so plan on that unless moonstone falls your way. Complete the structure before inserting a catalyst.

The Starlight Charger processes one material entry per operation. Run the cast and graded Tyrian Steel pickaxe head through three successful tier-three charges. Inspect it and continue until all three Tyrian Steel material entries have a Starlight charge level of at least three. Charging is the final operation on the loose part. Do not melt it afterward.

Assemble the charged head into a pickaxe, then apply the Overgeared finish to the completed tool. The quest checks all three charge values and final-tool quality.
