book.aoa.ascension_codex.welcome.name: Welcome
book.aoa.ascension_codex.welcome.descrip: The final age: Draconic Evolution endgame.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.welcome.where_y: The Otherworldly depths are cleared and the Ascension stage is in your hands. This is the final age: Draconic Evolution's endgame. The questbook walks the order; this dossier points to the final boss. Items from locked stages are intentionally hidden from EMI until their required progression unlocks. If an item is absent from EMI, that is the progression system working, not a glitch.
The boss ahead is stage-locked to Ascension: the Chaos Guardian, Draconic Evolution's final boss, found on a Chaos Island in the End. See the Bosses category for where to find it.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.bosses.name: Bosses
book.aoa.ascension_codex.bosses.descript: Where to find the boss that gates Ascension.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.bosses.chaos_gu: Where to Find the Chaos Guardian

From Draconic Evolution. The Chaos Guardian is the Ascension final boss, found on a Chaos Island in the End. Awaken the Chaos Crystal to draw it out; Guardian Crystals heal it like the Ender Dragon, so destroy them first. Stage-locked to Ascension.

A draconic final boss with guardian lasers, Wither adds, and projectiles. Break the Guardian Crystals, handle the Wither adds, and bring your absolute best kit. Drops Chaos Shards and the Dragon Heart.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.bosses.infernal: Block Factory's Bosses: Otherworldly dragon lane, not an Ascension gate.

From Block Factory's Bosses. Ashlord, the Infernal Dragon, is fought at a Dragon Tower, a surface structure in temperate Overworld biomes. It unlocks in the Otherworldly age and its quest lives in the Dragon Technology chapter there. Ascension does not wait on it. If you skipped the tower on the way up, it is still there to clear.

Ashlord fights alongside Ashlord Guards and flaming shooters. This pack runs it at 700 health behind 25 armor, up from the stock 250, with base damage raised a quarter. Clear the guards, manage the fire, and strike the dragon's exposed windows to land damage. Defeat drops Dragon Bones, used in Dragon Bones armor, plus other Block Factory reagents.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.luxtructo: Alex's Caves: walking-mountain apex of the Primordial Caves.

Luxtructosaurus lives inside the volcanoes that rise in the Primordial Caves, one of Alex's Caves' deep underground biomes. Find the biome first, then find a volcano in it. The beast sleeps in the volcano's core. To wake it you need an Ominous Catalyst, crafted from Heavy Bones and an Amber Curiosity you dig out of amber. Toss the Ominous Catalyst into the top of the volcano to trigger the eruption and raise the boss. Bring room to run and your best reactor-tier gear before you throw it. This is a required Atomic boss, stage-locked to the Atomic Age.

Luxtructosaurus is a walking mountain of an apex predator. It stomps, flings prey, and swings its tail, so keep distance and never get cornered against a wall. Chip it down while you stay mobile.

When it falls it drops Tectonic Shard in bulk. Collect the shards and turn them in at the quest to log the kill. This fight follows the Geburah exam and feeds forward into the Watcher, running Geburah into Luxtructosaurus into the Watcher into Tremorzilla, and the whole chain fans into the Atomic capstone.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.watcher.d: Alex's Caves: occult horror of the Abyssal Chasm.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.watcher.p:
The Watcher haunts the Abyssal Chasm, the flooded deep biome of Alex's Caves. It does not wander freely. Underzealots, the mole-like cultists down there, call it up through a Gloomoth Sacrifice to their dark god.

Go in deliberate and expect it to appear near that ritual. This is a required Atomic boss, stage-locked to the Atomic Age, and it comes right after the Luxtructosaurus kill.

The Watcher punishes carelessness and can possess its targets. Mind what it does when you look at it and control your approach rather than charging in. Deal with it on your terms.

Defeat it and take the Occult Gem, guaranteed on a real player kill. Hand the gem in at the quest. The Watcher feeds into Tremorzilla, which in turn drives the Atomic capstone, so it is the second-to-last link in the Atomic boss ladder.
book.aoa.atomic_dossier.bosses.tremorzil: Alex's Caves: the walking catastrophe that closes the Atomic Age.

Tremorzilla is not found. It is woken. You craft and hatch a Tremorzilla Egg using nuclear hellfire, then survive what climbs out. Keep the egg in mind as the trigger for the fight.

This is a required Atomic fight, not an optional deterrent. It is stage-locked to the Atomic Age and follows the Watcher in the boss ladder.

Tremorzilla is a walking catastrophe. It stomps, bites, swings its tail, and charges a radioactive beam that melts anything in its path. Break line of sight or move when it charges the beam, and never stand still. Your job is to survive and land steady damage.

Its kill feeds the Atomic capstone, the Chaos Gate at the end of the age, so the age does not close until Tremorzilla is down. It is the final link in the Geburah into Luxtructosaurus into the Watcher into Tremorzilla ladder.
book.aoa.gilded_ledger.bosses.malkuth.de: Qliphoth boss: the required Gilded exam.
book.aoa.gilded_ledger.bosses.malkuth.pa:
From FDBosses. Malkuth is one of the three Qliphoth bosses. You already fought Chesed back in the Industrial Revolution; Geburah waits in the Atomic Age. Malkuth is the required Gilded exam boss.

His arena generates in deep ocean biomes in the Overworld. Locate the Malkuth Arena, then summon him inside it with an Eye of Malkuth. Craft or acquire the eye during the Gilded factory lines and carry it to the arena.

The mod's developers recommend fighting Malkuth at night, so start the duel after dark. Bring full Gilded-tier gear and be ready for a long fight before you place the eye.

Malkuth cannot be hit directly. His divine armor negates normal damage, so you fight him through the cannons built into the arena. You are made weak to Fire or Ice, shown on your crosshair, and you may only fire the cannon that matches your current weakness. Match the cannon to the weakness, fire, and repeat while dodging his slashes, boulder volleys, and impaling spikes.

He drops the Fire and Ice Core, plus the Malkuth Trophy and the Emberfrost Gauntlet. The core is the kill proof the quest checks for.

Clearing Malkuth is the boss proof the handoff checks for, not a stage of its own. That proof is co-required into the Atomic Disassembler handoff, so this kill is part of what opens the Gilded to Atomic step alongside the Void Titan, the five factory lines, and the Chartered Arcana magic proof.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.theme.th: Why the Renaissance is the dimensions-and-magic turning point.

Earlier ages kept you on the overworld surface, mining down and building up. The Renaissance turns you outward. The Nether, the End, and Eternal Starlight are the required crossings of this age, each a separate world with its own materials and hazards. The Aether, the Undergarden, and the Otherside also become reachable, though their questlines wait for the Industrial Revolution.

This is why the Renaissance is the threshold age. Progression stops being one place. You are no longer improving a single base. You are learning to reach, survive, and return from worlds that each want something different from you.

The magic mods activate in the same age the dimensions do. Blood & Brimstone runs Malum, Occultism, Theurgy, and the Neo Vitae Ara Vitae up to the Tabula Vitae. Prisms & Circles runs Spectrum color work and the required Mahou Tsukai line. Forbidden Arcanus stays optional flavor with no required quests.

That pairing is deliberate. Exploration hands you strange materials, and magic is the craft that turns them into power. Soulstone and spirits feed Malum's altar. Blood and life essence run Neo Vitae. The dimensions supply the reagents, and the magic lines consume them. Neither half stands alone.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.theme.de: Why the Renaissance runs three waves and a finale, and how to pace it.

The Renaissance is the widest age in the pack, but it is not a pile of separate chapters. It runs in waves. Master of the Grove opens three chapters at once: Blood & Brimstone, Steam & Ledger, and Prisms & Circles. Work them in any order.

Each one ends on a capstone: the Nether Gauntlet, The Complete Record, and the Mystic Code. Those three meet at Three Roads Converge, which opens The Transmutation Hall and its Blast Brick. The Blast Brick opens the finale trio, and clearing all three grants the next age. That chain is the gate, not a checklist of chapters.

Density is the point, not an accident. Three parallel disciplines and a deep alchemy hall cannot be compressed into a short age without cutting content, so the Renaissance is built wide on purpose. Expect to spend real time here.

Work the three wave chapters in parallel. Many reagents and materials arrive as rewards from milestones in one lane and feed another, so progress spreads. Keep the wave capstones moving, take optional magic depth when you want it, and treat the age as a long stretch rather than a sprint. The Aether, Undergarden, and Otherside are optional frontier now; their guided questlines belong to the next age.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.troubles: Each dimension needs its own portal or access item.

The Renaissance makes several dimensions reachable, and each one is entered a different way. There is no universal portal. If you are stuck, you are probably using the wrong access method for that dimension.

The Nether uses the vanilla obsidian portal lit with flint and steel, and its required work is the Nether wing of Blood & Brimstone. The Aether is reached through a glowstone frame filled with a water bucket, not lit with fire. Its islands float over open void, so bring blocks to bridge with. The Aether is optional frontier now; its guided questline opens in the Industrial Revolution.

Eternal Starlight is not built from scratch. You find half-collapsed Common Portal Ruins in the overworld and repair one to open the crossing. Starlight is a required finale chapter, so this crossing matters for age progress.

The Undergarden portal is a built frame opened by throwing a crafted Catalyst at it rather than using flint and steel. The Otherside comes from Deeper Darker, built from a frame inside an Ancient City and activated with a Heart of the Deep. Both are reachable now, but their guided questlines belong to the Industrial Revolution. Match the access item to the dimension and the crossing will open.
End Remastered replaces the eye portal with distinct earned eyes.

If you throw a vanilla Eye of Ender expecting it to point toward a stronghold, nothing happens. End Remastered changes how the End is reached. Vanilla eyes cannot be thrown in this pack.

Instead the mod fills the portal with distinct EndRem eyes that you earn across Renaissance. The portal frame in a stronghold stays dormant until twelve eyes are seated.

The End Threshold quest batch tracks ten obtainable eyes: Magical, Nether, Corrupted, Cursed, Cold, Lost, Undead, Old, Black, and Rogue. Undead is renewable by craft. Evil and Cryptic eyes are disabled in End Remastered config and cannot be obtained.

The portal still needs twelve frames. Fill the remaining frames with other obtainable EndRem eyes such as Exotic, Witch, or Guardian. Several tracked eyes arrive as quest rewards, so check your reward pile before hunting. Once you hold enough eyes for twelve frames, throw an End Remastered eye to locate a stronghold, then seat every eye in the frame to open the End.

The vanilla enchanting table works now that you have reached diamond tier and the Renaissance. Ring it with bookshelves for higher levels. Apotheosis later adds shelves that push past the fifteen-shelf vanilla cap, but the plain table is available to you immediately.

Enchant your gear before you seat the last eye. The End fight punishes weak equipment, so spend your levels on a bow, armor, and a solid melee weapon while you still have a calm base to work in. Once the portal is lit, there is no quick trip back for supplies.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.mods.mag: The Neo Vitae line ends on the Tabula Vitae inside Blood & Brimstone.

Neo Vitae (neovitae) is the required magic line of Blood & Brimstone. Build the Ara Vitae blood altar through Weak and Apprentice orbs and Blank Runes, then craft the Tabula Vitae transmutation workbench. That craft closes the Neo Vitae line.

Malum, Occultism, and Theurgy run alongside it in the same chapter. Their own lines teach the stations that the later alchemy in The Transmutation Hall will need. Work each line to its close as you push the chapter toward its Nether Gauntlet capstone.
Runes, Tabula Vitae, And Later Work

Once the Ara Vitae runs, place Blank Runes around it in the patterns shown in Neo Vitae's own guidebook to raise its tier. Higher tiers unlock stronger orbs and larger recipes.

The Tabula Vitae is the Renaissance close for this line, not the pinnacle of all pack magic. The Athanor arrives in the Industrial Revolution, built from an Industrial Tabula Animata. Deeper Neo Vitae gear, the Hellforged chain, and the Sentient armor line continue in the industrial ages. Spectrum is taught in Prisms & Circles, not in this chapter.
Blood & Brimstone magic plus Prisms & Circles at the Renaissance.

Blood & Brimstone runs four magic lines. Build each first station, then work that line to its close.

Malum (malum): the Spirit Altar, spirit harvest, and the Harvest of Souls close. Theurgy (theurgy): the Calcination Oven, Liquefaction Cauldron, and the Sal Ammoniac Tank close. Occultism (occultism): the Dictionary of Spirits, Golden Ritual Bowl, Foliot binding, and the Transporter Book of Calling close. Neo Vitae (neovitae): the Ara Vitae up to the Tabula Vitae.

Spectrum (spectrum) runs in Prisms & Circles. Start with Basic Gem Pedestals, then climb the pedestal tiers up to the Onyx pedestal, which is where Spectrum ends in the Renaissance. The Moonstone pedestal and the crystal growing that follows it are Atomic-age steps, not this age. The Pigment Palette and Fusion Shrine come later in the chapter.

Mahou Tsukai (mahoutsukai) is the required line of this chapter, not optional depth. Begin with the Knowledge Compendium and the Attuner, where attuned gems store mana. Spell scrolls come from ritual circles, and the Mystic Code stores and casts them. The Mystic Code is the Prisms & Circles capstone. Forbidden Arcanus stays optional flavor with no required quests.

These mods run deep, and their higher tiers are staged to later ages. Do not expect them yet.

Occultism's Djinni summoning and its automation open at the Industrial Revolution, with Marid summoning held back to the Otherworldly age. Theurgy's Digestion Vat and Forbidden Arcanus's Aureal Tank both unlock at the Industrial Revolution. Finish the Renaissance magic lines now, then return for the advanced apparatus once the next age begins.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.mods.dim: Eternal Starlight is a required finale; the Aether is optional frontier.

The Aether (aether) is a floating sky realm reached through a glowstone frame filled with a water bucket. The dimension and its guided questline, Aether Literacy, both open in the Renaissance.

Start with Skyroot tools and Holystone, then mine Zanite Ore for Zanite Gemstones and craft a Zanite Axe. Use that axe to harvest Golden Amber from Golden Oak Logs. A Bronze Dungeon houses the Slider boss, whose Bronze Key opens the reward vault. The Silver Dungeon holds the Valkyrie Queen, a required Renaissance boss, so build toward that fight this age rather than deferring it.

Eternal Starlight (eternal_starlight) is a dim, dreamlike dimension reached by repairing a Common Portal Ruin found in the overworld. Its questline, Starlight Observation, is a required finale chapter of the Renaissance.

Inside you will find unique woods, the Starcore, and Aethersent Ingot. The chapter's required boss is the Starlight Golem, which drops the Forge Armor Trim template you turn in to close the chapter. The Gatekeeper is a second Starlight boss you can take for its own loot. Starlight is one of the three finale gates, so its work counts toward the next age.
The Undergarden and the Otherside are optional frontier; their questlines are next age.

The Undergarden (undergarden) is a lush underground world reached with a crafted Catalyst thrown at a built portal frame. The dimension is stage-locked to the Industrial Revolution, so the portal will not carry you through before then. Its guided questline, the Undergarden Descent, opens at the same time.

Mine Cloggrum, Utheric Shard, and Forgotten Ingot, and watch for the Utheric Infection, a status effect that spreads if you let it. Treat the Undergarden as optional frontier. Read the route now and plan the trip for next age.

Deeper Darker (deeperdarker) extends the vanilla Deep Dark and opens the Otherside dimension below bedrock. Reinforce an Echo Shard into a Reinforced Echo Shard, the key material for reaching and surviving down there.

The Otherside is a sculk realm of Warden Carapace, the Heart of the Deep, and Resonarium. The dimension is stage-locked to the Industrial Revolution, so the portal will not carry you through before then. Its guided questline, the Deeper Darker Otherside, opens at the same time. Study the route now and plan the descent for next age.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.mods.net: Vanilla Nether and End open, plus Apotheosis and End Remastered.

The vanilla Nether and End are gated to the Renaissance in this pack. They do not open in the Dark Ages. The Nether's required work is the Nether wing of Blood & Brimstone: light an obsidian portal, gather blaze rods and powder from a Nether Fortress, and forge a Blaze Burner.

That same blaze work feeds the Gauntlet fight in its Nether arena, and the Blaze Burner carries forward as a steam heat source in Steam & Ledger. Plan a full Nether trip, not a quick dip.

End Remastered (endrem) replaces the vanilla End portal. The portal still needs twelve eyes seated in its frames. The End Threshold quest batch tracks ten obtainable eyes, including Undead, with renewable crafts for recovery. Evil and Cryptic eyes are disabled in config.

Fill the remaining frames with other obtainable EndRem eyes such as Exotic, Witch, or Guardian. The End Threshold chapter lists the tracked set and the recovery routes. This turns reaching the End into a long exploration goal without softlocking on a consumed eye.

Apotheosis (apotheosis) comes online as a support layer during the Renaissance and runs for the rest of the pack. It adds affix loot, gem sockets, and enchanting depth on top of your gear.

Collect Gem Dust and gem materials from tiered mobs, then use a Sigil of Socketing to add sockets and slot gems into weapons and armor. Apotheosis is not gated behind a station. It rewards you passively as you fight and loot, so read affixes on drops before you scrap them.
book.aoa.renaissance_compendium.mods.sil: Silent Gear and Silent Gear Metalworks
Modular tool parts, alloy tiers, and the shared foundry casting bridge.

Every Silent Gear tool starts with a pattern. Fold four paper and one blue dye into blueprint paper, a reusable pattern stock, or right-click a log with a knife to cut template boards for a free but single-use option. Shape either one with a wooden rod into a part-specific blueprint or template, one recipe per gear type: a sword blueprint, a pickaxe blueprint, and so on.

Combine that blueprint or template with materials at a crafting table to make the tool's main part. A sword blade takes two materials, a pickaxe head takes three, a shovel head takes one. The bench only accepts materials that Silent Gear Metalworks leaves out of the casting group, which means wood, stone, flint, bone, and the other non-meltable entries. Iron, copper, gold, diamond, and every alloy are casting materials and the bench recipe rejects them. Those parts come out of the foundry instead, and page three walks that route.

Rods and tips carry the same restriction, so bench-craft those from wood or stone. Combine a head and a rod at the crafting table to finish a tool. Bindings, grips, cords, linings, fletching, coatings, and adornments are untouched and still accept any material that fits the slot. Every tool also has a quick recipe that folds blueprint, materials, and rod into the finished tool in one craft, under the same casting-material restriction.

Silent Gear's strongest materials are alloys, not mined ore. Crimson Iron and Azure Silver are the two mined ones, from the Nether and the End. Blaze Gold is the entry alloy and comes off a plain crafting table from one gold ingot and four blaze powder. All three, along with their ingots, nuggets, dust, and blocks, become available at the Renaissance, and the Material Grader opens with them.

Later ages add stronger alloys on top of those three. Crimson Steel unlocks at the Industrial Revolution and takes four Crimson Iron ingots, two blaze rods, and a magma cream at the crafting table. Azure Electrum and Tyrian Steel wait for the Gilded Age. Azure Electrum takes four Azure Silver ingots, two gold ingots, and an ender pearl. Tyrian Steel has no crafting-table recipe at all: it is made only on the Alloy Forge, from Crimson Steel, Azure Electrum, a crushed shulker shell, and netherite scrap. This pack adds a faster station route to each of the four alloys as well, and the book for the age that owns the station explains it.

No stage lock stands between you and the base mod. Blueprints, templates, the stone anvil, and the salvager are open from the moment you can reach this book, and so are wood, stone, flint, and bone parts. Iron, copper, and diamond parts are reachable too, but only through the foundry, because Metalworks marks them for casting. The larger stations are staged with the tiers they serve. The Material Grader is Renaissance, the Alloy Forge Industrial Revolution, the Metal Press Atomic, and the Starlight Charger Otherworldly. Silent Gear runs as its own forging ladder in this pack, and no rung on it gates an age, so build with it when it fits your playstyle.
The Shared Forge Bridge, Grading, and Salvage

The Productive Metalworks foundry, the same one from the Metallurgy chapter's Coke and Casting line, is not an optional shortcut for Silent Gear. It is the only way to make a metal or gem part. Silent Gear Metalworks marks every meltable material as a casting material and strips those materials out of the crafting-table recipes for heads, rods, and tips, so the bench builds parts only from wood, stone, flint, and bone. The route runs in two steps. Bench-craft a part from one of those materials, set it on the Casting Table, and pour 360 millibuckets of molten steel over it. That pour consumes the part and hands back a reusable cast. Then melt the material you actually want, put the cast on the table, and pour again to stamp out the real part. A pickaxe head takes three material units, a sword blade two. One limit to know: this pack removes the foundry's direct alloying recipes for Blaze Gold, Crimson Steel, Azure Electrum, and Tyrian Steel, so make those alloys by their own routes and melt the finished ingots.

Two more stations round out the mod, both optional. The Material Grader takes a catalyst dust, glowing, blazing, or glittery, and rerolls a material's quality grade; higher grades make stronger parts from the same base material. The Salvager breaks vanilla tools, armor, and old Silent Gear parts back into their component materials, so you can recover what you do not want anymore. Neither station gates anything forward; they are quality-of-life loops for players who want to keep optimizing their gear.

book.aoa.ascension_codex.mechanics.table: Extended Crafting fusion and the ultimate table.

Ascension runs on two crafting surfaces that dwarf anything from earlier ages. Extended Crafting supplies the tiered grid tables and the fusion system; Avaritia supplies the compression and Extreme Crafting path. You need both by the end of the age, so build the entry pieces of each before you chase the reactor.

Extended Crafting climbs Basic, Advanced, Elite, then Ultimate Crafting Table. The Advanced Crafting Table is stage-locked to Ascension in this pack, so do not expect it earlier. Each tier unlocks a larger grid and accepts the recipes the next tier of gear needs.

The second Extended Crafting system is the Crafting Core. Place a Crafting Core and surround it with Pedestals within a three block radius on the same Y level. The center item goes on the core and the surrounding items go on the pedestals. Feed the core power, because the recipe will not run without it.

The core is not instant. Right click the side of the core to see progress, stored power, and power cost. If a craft stalls, the core is usually short on power, not missing a recipe. The tiered tables above still handle most of the age's recipes, so use the Crafting Core for the specific combination recipes that call for it.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.mechanics.neutr: Avaritia compression and the Extreme Crafting Table.

Avaritia's spine is compression. The Neutronium Collector gathers cosmic material over time, and the Neutronium Compressor packs stacks of an input down into a single denser output. This is slow by design. Set the collector and compressor running early and let them work in the background while you build the reactor.

The compression path produces the singularities and the Crystal Matrix stock that the Extreme recipes consume. There is no shortcut that skips the wait.

The Extreme Crafting Table is Avaritia's nine-by-nine grid. It is where the Infinity Catalyst and the final Infinity path are assembled from compressed materials. It is a plain crafting surface with a huge grid, so it needs no power, only the right ingredients in the right slots.

The Ascension quest line points the Avaritia path at the Eternal Singularity and Infinity Catalyst. Feed the collectors, run the compressors, and keep the Extreme Table stocked so the capstone is not waiting on raw neutronium.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.mechanics.silen: Tier-five grading for the final Tyrian Steel tool.

Use Draconic Fusion Crafting to produce Awakened Draconium. This pack registers the ingot as a tier-five Material Grader catalyst.

Use it to re-grade the prepared Tyrian Steel head. Continue only while the grader can improve the part. The final proof requires all three recorded Tyrian Steel material grades to equal MAX.

Keep charge level three or higher on all three material entries while improving the head's grade. Do not remelt the part. Assemble the pickaxe after all three grades reach MAX, then finish the completed tool with quartz on the Overgeared anvil.

The final quest checks three MAX grades, three charge values at level three or higher, and recorded Overgeared forging quality.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.reactor.require: Required win-gate. The quest checks placement, not operation.

The Draconic Reactor from Draconic Evolution is not optional. It is a required Ascension win-gate multiblock, so treat it as progression rather than a side project.

Know exactly what the quest asks. The Impossible Machine chapter uses place-block checks on one Draconic Reactor Core, one Reactor Energy Injector, and one Reactor Stabilizer. Setting those three blocks down completes it. The quest does not inspect the assembled multiblock and does not check that the reactor ever runs.

A working reactor needs more than that, and the pages that follow are the build and the safety brief for actually lighting one.

Place the Reactor Core with empty space all around it. Set four Reactor Stabilizers facing the core, spaced evenly on opposite sides, and link each one to the core. Place the Reactor Energy Injector facing the core as well and run a real power feed into it. The Injector supplies containment power only. It does not accept reactor fuel.

Load fuel through the Reactor Core interface, not the Injector. Press Charge and keep power going in until charging finishes, then press Activate. The reactor produces nothing useful until the containment field is up and core temperature has climbed into its running band.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.reactor.reactor: Containment power, the readouts, and a controlled stop.

A Draconic Reactor is a controlled explosion. The Stabilizers project a containment field, and the Reactor Energy Injector is what powers that field. If Containment Field Strength reaches zero while the core is hot, the reactor breaches and levels a large area. Never let the field starve.

The Reactor Core interface shows Core Temperature, Containment Field Strength, Energy Saturation, and Fuel Conversion Level. Field Input Rate tells you the exact power draw the current field needs, and it climbs steeply as strength rises. Rising temperature with falling field strength is the failure spiral.

The reactor makes far more power than it consumes once it is running, but the Injector has to keep feeding the field the whole time. Build a large buffer before you light it. The Energy Core with Energy Core Stabilizers, driven through Energy Pylons and managed by the Draconic Energy Controller, is the intended sink and source. Route reactor output into that buffer and feed containment power back out of it.

Stop it with the Shutdown button in the Reactor Core interface. The core cools and finishes the stop once temperature and saturation reach the shutdown conditions, and Semi-Automated Shutdown can trigger that for you below 2500C at 99 percent saturation. Cutting fuel is not an emergency brake. If the field is falling, push power at the Injector and use the controls. Site your first reactor well away from your base and your Energy Core.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.capstone.dracon: Chaotic tier: chaos crafting past awakened gear.

The Draconic Heart chapter takes fusion crafting up to the Chaotic tier. Below it sits the awakened tier, built on the Draconic Fusion Crafting Injector and Draconic Cores. Chaotic gear is the top rung, and it demands Chaos Shards won from the Chaos Guardian in the End.

Chaotic recipes run through the Chaotic Fusion Crafting Injector and the Chaotic Core. These injectors draw even more power per craft than the awakened ones, so the reactor buffer you built pays off here directly.

Draconic Additions extends this tier with the Chaos Liquifier and the Chaos Infuser. Feed Chaos Shards into the Chaos Liquifier to build up Liquid Chaos, then use that stored chaos in the Chaos Infuser to turn a Dragon Heart into a Chaos Heart. The Chaos Heart is the key part for the top endgame gear and modules. This is where Chaos Shard drops become usable power rather than trophies.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.capstone.archiv: The Ultimate Block, the Infinity Ingot, and aoa_complete.

The final chapter converges everything. The Archive of Ages step assembles The Ultimate Block from Extended Crafting, the single most expensive compressed craft in the pack. Every earlier tier of table, catalyst, and component funnels into it. Completing it grants the archive proof and unlocks the last step.

Do not start this until both crafting spines are mature. The Ultimate Block wants the top outputs of the fusion system, and those want a running reactor for power.

The last craft turns The Ultimate Block into the Infinity Ingot on the Avaritia path. Completing that quest fires the final grants: it seals your run and awards the aoa_complete stage. That stage is the end of the eight-age climb.

Before this, the finale boss must fall. The Chaos Guardian on its Chaos Island is the only fight this age gates, and Bosses Rise is that fight and nothing else. Scylla, the Kraken, and the Infernal Dragon are Otherworldly lane work and no longer stand in the way. Finish the guardian, finish both crafting spines, forge the Infinity Ingot, and Ascension is complete.
book.aoa.ascension_codex.troubleshooting: Fusion stalls, dead compressors, and reactor faults.

If a fusion craft never completes, the Crafting Core is underpowered. The Pedestals only hold items; all energy goes into the Core itself, so confirm the Core has a live power feed and let it fill before you start. If an Avaritia recipe refuses to craft, check that you are using the Extreme Crafting Table and that every neutronium input is compressed to the exact tier the recipe names.

If the collectors and compressors seem dead, they are usually just slow. Compression is deliberately gradual; leave them running and check back.

A reactor that will not start almost always has an incomplete multiblock. Confirm four Stabilizers are placed and linked and that the Reactor Energy Injector faces the core. If field strength collapses when you activate or raise output, the power feed into the containment field is too small. Enlarge the buffer and the injector feed before trying again.

If a stage-locked table or block will not craft, the Ascension stage may not be granted yet. The Advanced Crafting Table and the final surfaces unlock with Ascension, so finish the questbook order rather than working around the lock.
